### PQB_T1_MSQ_01: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 1, select all historical milestones established in animal histology: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Xavier Bichat classified 21 tissue types without microscope
- [ ] B) Marcello Malpighi pioneered microscopic tissue investigation
- [ ] C) Mayer coined the formal term 'Histology'
- [ ] D) True tissue level first evolved in Phylum Coelenterata
- [ ] E) Anton van Leeuwenhoek discovered the Haversian osteon system

> **✅ Answers:** A) Xavier Bichat classified 21 tissue types without microscope, B) Marcello Malpighi pioneered microscopic tissue investigation, C) Mayer coined the formal term 'Histology', D) True tissue level first evolved in Phylum Coelenterata
> **Explanation:** Bichat, Malpighi, Mayer, and Coelenterate evolution represent foundational histology milestones.

### PQB_T1_MSQ_02: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 1, select all primary tissue classes found in complex animals: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Epithelial Tissue
- [ ] B) Connective Tissue
- [ ] C) Muscular Tissue
- [ ] D) Nervous Tissue
- [ ] E) Vascular Tissue as separate primary class

> **✅ Answers:** A) Epithelial Tissue, B) Connective Tissue, C) Muscular Tissue, D) Nervous Tissue
> **Explanation:** 4 primary tissues: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular, Nervous.

### PQB_T1_MSQ_03: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 1, select all embryonic germ layers that give rise to Epithelial Tissues: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Ectoderm (Skin epidermis)
- [ ] B) Mesoderm (Endothelium & Mesothelium)
- [ ] C) Endoderm (GI tract mucosa)
- [ ] D) Neural crest only
- [ ] E) Blastoderm only

> **✅ Answers:** A) Ectoderm (Skin epidermis), B) Mesoderm (Endothelium & Mesothelium), C) Endoderm (GI tract mucosa)
> **Explanation:** Epithelial tissue arises from Ectoderm, Mesoderm, and Endoderm.


<br/><img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="From Question Bank perspective, in Topic" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" /><br/>

### PQB_T1_MSQ_04: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 1, select all components forming the epithelial basement membrane: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Basal lamina secreted by epithelial cells
- [ ] B) Reticular lamina secreted by connective tissue
- [ ] C) Type IV Collagen and Laminin glycoproteins
- [ ] D) Reticular collagen fibers and Perlecan
- [ ] E) Mineralized calcium phosphate crystals

> **✅ Answers:** A) Basal lamina secreted by epithelial cells, B) Reticular lamina secreted by connective tissue, C) Type IV Collagen and Laminin glycoproteins, D) Reticular collagen fibers and Perlecan
> **Explanation:** Basement membrane comprises basal lamina and reticular lamina rich in Type IV collagen, laminin, and perlecan.

### PQB_T1_MSQ_05: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 1, select all true statements regarding biological organization hierarchy: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Cells assemble into functional tissues
- [ ] B) Tissues combine to form organs
- [ ] C) Organs cooperate within organ systems
- [ ] D) Organ systems constitute the intact organism
- [ ] E) Organs assemble directly into tissues

> **✅ Answers:** A) Cells assemble into functional tissues, B) Tissues combine to form organs, C) Organs cooperate within organ systems, D) Organ systems constitute the intact organism
> **Explanation:** Biological hierarchy progresses: Cell -> Tissue -> Organ -> Organ System -> Organism.

### PQB_T1_MSQ_06: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 1, select all tissues derived exclusively from embryonic Mesoderm: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Loose and Dense Connective Tissues
- [ ] B) Skeletal, Smooth, and Cardiac Muscles
- [ ] C) Vascular Blood and Bone tissues
- [ ] D) Dermis of skin and Cartilage
- [ ] E) Central Nervous System neurones

> **✅ Answers:** A) Loose and Dense Connective Tissues, B) Skeletal, Smooth, and Cardiac Muscles, C) Vascular Blood and Bone tissues, D) Dermis of skin and Cartilage
> **Explanation:** Connective tissues, muscle types, bone, blood, and dermis originate from mesoderm.

### PQB_T1_MSQ_07: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 1, select all key histological characteristics of Epithelial Tissue: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Tightly packed cells with minimal intercellular matrix
- [ ] B) Avascular nature (lacks direct blood vessels)
- [ ] C) High regenerative and mitotic capacity
- [ ] D) Rests upon non-cellular basement membrane
- [ ] E) Abundant vascular matrix separating cells

> **✅ Answers:** A) Tightly packed cells with minimal intercellular matrix, B) Avascular nature (lacks direct blood vessels), C) High regenerative and mitotic capacity, D) Rests upon non-cellular basement membrane
> **Explanation:** Epithelial tissue is tightly packed, avascular, highly regenerative, and rests on a basement membrane.

### PQB_T1_MSQ_08: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 1, select all specialized structural functions of epithelial coverings: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Physical protection against mechanical abrasion
- [ ] B) Barrier against pathogen entry
- [ ] C) Prevention of fluid desiccation
- [ ] D) Trans-epithelial selective absorption and secretion
- [ ] E) High-force mechanical tendon traction

> **✅ Answers:** A) Physical protection against mechanical abrasion, B) Barrier against pathogen entry, C) Prevention of fluid desiccation, D) Trans-epithelial selective absorption and secretion
> **Explanation:** Epithelia protect, block pathogens, prevent drying, and regulate absorption/secretion.

### PQB_T1_MSQ_09: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 1, select all organisms demonstrating tissue-level grade of organization: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Hydra (Coelenterata)
- [ ] B) Aurelia jellyfish (Cnidaria)
- [ ] C) Metridium sea anemone (Cnidaria)
- [ ] D) Sponges (Porifera)
- [ ] E) Amoeba (Protozoa)

> **✅ Answers:** A) Hydra (Coelenterata), B) Aurelia jellyfish (Cnidaria), C) Metridium sea anemone (Cnidaria)
> **Explanation:** Coelenterates (Hydra, Aurelia, Metridium) exhibit tissue-level organization. Sponges display cellular grade.

### PQB_T1_MSQ_10: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 1, select all pathways by which avascular epithelial cells receive oxygen and nutrients: (Select all that apply)

- [ ] A) Simple diffusion from underlying connective tissue capillaries
- [ ] B) Trans-basement membrane nutrient transport
- [ ] C) Intercellular gap junction metabolite sharing
- [ ] D) Direct intra-epithelial arteriolar blood flow
- [ ] E) Perichondrial canaliculi mineral transport

> **✅ Answers:** A) Simple diffusion from underlying connective tissue capillaries, B) Trans-basement membrane nutrient transport, C) Intercellular gap junction metabolite sharing
> **Explanation:** Avascular epithelial cells receive nutrients via diffusion across the basement membrane from CT capillaries.
